paper: What Supercomputers Say: A Study of Five System Logs
detector: Empirical characterization; not a LAD model
potential_gap: Primary provenance and label semantics for BGL
notes: Cite together with Loghub when using BGL

paper: Learning from Time-Changing Data with Adaptive Windowing
metrics: False positives; false negatives; predictive performance
limitations: Not log-specific; often monitors error and may require labels
potential_gap: Provides a naive drift-trigger baseline but not log-drift characterization
notes: Use ADWIN as optional comparator on a scalar signal

paper: A Survey on Concept Drift Adaptation
drift_type: Real and virtual; sudden; gradual; recurring
limitations: Strict concept drift often concerns changing P(Y|X)
potential_gap: For this thesis distinguish virtual/log-distribution drift from real concept drift

paper: Drain: An Online Log Parsing Approach with Fixed Depth Tree
dataset: Five real-world log datasets; over 10M messages
representation: Online templates from fixed-depth parse tree
drift_detection: Online clustering; not a drift detector
limitations: Parser output can itself change and confound measured emergence
potential_gap: Freeze parser version/config and audit template churn separately

paper: DeepLog: Anomaly Detection and Diagnosis from System Logs through Deep Learning
adaptation: Operator feedback/model update discussed but no drift-aware policy
limitations: Assumes learned normal sequence regime; unseen evolution can raise alarms
potential_gap: Suitable published detector behind a detector-agnostic policy

paper: Robust Log-Based Anomaly Detection on Unstable Log Data
dataset: HDFS with injected evolution/noise and Microsoft service logs
drift_type: Unstable events/sequences from evolution and processing noise
adaptation: Representation robustness rather than an explicit adapt decision
limitations: Robustness is not a whether/when adaptation policy
potential_gap: Compare robustness against active adaptation; separate representation from policy

paper: LogAnomaly: Unsupervised Detection of Sequential and Quantitative Anomalies in Unstructured Logs
drift_detection: Template similarity; no explicit drift episodes
adaptation: Approximate new templates to existing vectors; periodic retraining context
limitations: Handles new templates through approximation rather than deciding when adaptation is justified
potential_gap: Strong main-detector alternative; policy gap remains

paper: Learning under Concept Drift: A Review
potential_gap: Supports treating characterization as drift understanding before adaptation
notes: Framework aligns with RQ2 to RQ3 chain

paper: HitAnomaly: Hierarchical Transformers for Anomaly Detection in System Log
representation: Template sequence semantics and parameter values
adaptation: Robust model representation; no explicit policy
limitations: Model-centric and computationally heavier; no AD/FAR
potential_gap: Candidate secondary detector if resources permit

paper: LogBERT: Log Anomaly Detection via BERT
limitations: Focuses detector quality rather than evolving-regime decisions
potential_gap: Useful secondary detector but outside minimum scope

paper: Log-based Anomaly Detection with Deep Learning: How Far Are We?
drift_type: Dataset and evaluation variation rather than explicit drift episodes
limitations: Shows results are sensitive to data and evaluation choices
potential_gap: Motivates one frozen protocol shared across all policies

paper: LogEncoder: Log-Based Contrastive Representation Learning for Anomaly Detection
representation: Pretrained semantic vectors; contrastive and one-class objectives
drift_type: Distribution shift not the primary experimental object
drift_detection: Online/offline detection modes; no explicit drift characterization
limitations: Representation learning focus; no controlled adaptation timing
potential_gap: Possible detector alternative; not the thesis contribution

paper: Robust and Transferable Log-based Anomaly Detection
dataset: Large real-world log datasets across environments
representation: Multiple log fields and invariant representations
drift_detection: Environment generalization rather than online episode detection
limitations: Avoids adaptation through invariant learning; does not evaluate whether/when to update

paper: LogOnline: A Semi-supervised Log-based Anomaly Detector Aided with Online Learning Mechanism
drift_type: Log instability and dissimilar new events
drift_detection: High-confidence normality selection before online updates
adaptation: Continuous one-iteration online weight updates without labels/human intervention
limitations: Official abstract and OMLog's method comparison describe continuous updating; neither source reports AD/FAR or explicit transient/no-drift controls
potential_gap: Differentiate explicit decision layer and false-adaptation controls
notes: Official ASE abstract reviewed; mechanism cross-checked in OMLog full text

paper: EvLog: Identifying Anomalous Logs over Software Evolution
drift_type: Evolving events; parser errors; unstable sequences
adaptation: Robust detection across versions rather than model-update timing
limitations: Targets individual anomalous logs and robustness rather than adaptation decisions
potential_gap: Use as strongest evidence that software evolution matters; policy gap remains

paper: Loghub: A Large Collection of System Log Datasets for AI-driven Log Analytics
potential_gap: Authoritative BGL distribution; licensing and citation source

paper: LogSD: Detecting Anomalies from System Logs through Self-Supervised Learning and Frequency-Based Masking
drift_type: Not explicitly modeled as temporal drift

paper: OMLog: Online Log Anomaly Detection for Evolving System with Meta-learning
adaptation: Conditionally switches online meta-learning versus offline fast inference
temporal_evaluation: Stable HDFS and evolved BGL; five independent runs
limitations: Full text reports F1 and efficiency plus threshold sensitivity; it does not define adaptation delay/FAR or controlled transient/no-drift update controls
potential_gap: Novelty emphasizes multi-signal characterization and explicit AD/FAR/no-adapt protocol rather than conditional adaptation itself
notes: Full arXiv v1 methods and evaluation reviewed 2026-09-25

paper: Log-based Anomaly Detection for Evolving Software: An Incremental Deep-learning Approach
drift_detection: Threshold on proportion of changed templates
adaptation: Partial fine-tuning with herding or knowledge distillation
limitations: Closest published work; official article describes a changed-template-proportion trigger but does not expose AD/FAR or controlled transient/no-drift policy tests
